formulations.label: Mouthwash (oromucosal solution)
formulations.note: Two UK 0.2% mouthwash SmPCs (peppermint and original flavour) have the same clinical content. Not intended to be swallowed.

src.q: Chlorhexidine Digluconate 0.2% w/v
Oromucosal solution
Chlorhexidine Digluconate 0.2% w/v
[This product is not intended to be swallowed]

bnf.note: BNF/BNFC is only available in the UK; not accessed.

items.t: Inhibition of dental plaque; aid in treating and preventing gingivitis and in oral hygiene when toothbrushing is not possible (e.g. after oral surgery).

src.q: For inhibition of the formation of dental plaque.
As an aid in the treatment and prevention of gingivitis and in the maintenance of oral hygiene, particularly in situations where toothbrushing cannot be adequately employed

items.t: Post-periodontal surgery or treatment, to promote gingival healing (studied only over the short term).

src.q: Also for use in a post-periodontal surgery or treatment* regimen to promote gingival healing.
Use as part of a post-periodontal treatment regimen has only been adequately studied over the short term

items.t: Useful in aphthous ulceration and oral candidal infections (e.g. denture stomatitis and thrush).

src.q: It is useful in the management of aphthous ulceration and oral candidal infections (e.g. denture stomatitis and thrush).

restrictions.note: No prescribing restrictions found in the two UK 0.2% mouthwash SmPCs (general sale) or MHRA Drug Safety Update.

items.t: Adults: rinse the mouth thoroughly for about 1 minute with 10 mL twice daily, then spit out. Do not exceed the stated dose.

src.q: Thoroughly rinse the mouth for about one minute with 10 ml twice daily. Spit out after use.
Do not exceed the stated dose.

items.t: Gingivitis: a course of about one month is advisable.

src.q: For the treatment of gingivitis a course of about one month is advisable

items.t: Aphthous ulceration and oral candidal infections: continue for 48 hours after clinical resolution.

src.q: In the case of aphthous ulceration and oral candidal infections treatment should be continued for 48 hours after clinical resolution.

items.t: Denture stomatitis: clean the dentures and soak them in the mouthwash for 15 minutes twice daily.

src.q: For the treatment of dental stomatitis the dentures should be cleansed and soaked in

items.t: Dental surgery: rinse for 1 minute before treatment.

src.q: In the dental surgery the patient should be instructed to rinse the mouth for one minute prior to treatment.

items.t: Children 12 years and over: adult dose. Under 12 years: should not use unless recommended by a healthcare professional.

src.q: The normal adult dose is appropriate for elderly patients and children of 12 years and over unless otherwise recommended by the dentist or the physician.
Children under 12 years of age should not use the product unless recommended by a healthcare professional.

items.t: Previous hypersensitivity reaction to chlorhexidine or to any excipient.

src.q: is contraindicated for patients who have previously shown a hypersensitivity reaction to Chlorhexidine or to any of the excipients in the formulation
Corsodyl is contraindicated for patients who have previously shown a hypersensitivity reaction to Chlorhexidine or to any of the excipients in the formulation.

items.t: MHRA: chlorhexidine can cause generalised allergic reactions and anaphylactic shock; do not give any chlorhexidine product to anyone with a possible history of allergic reaction to chlorhexidine.

src.q: chlorhexidine is known to induce hypersensitivity, including generalised allergic reactions and anaphylactic shock
Products or medical devices containing chlorhexidine should not be administered to anyone with a possible history of an allergic reaction to chlorhexidine.

items.t: For mouth use only: do not swallow; keep out of the eyes and ears (wash eyes out promptly and thoroughly with water if splashed).

src.q: For oromucosal use only. Do not swallow. Keep out of the eyes and ears.
If the mouthwash comes into contact with the eyes, wash out promptly and thoroughly with water.

items.t: Tooth and tongue staining may occur; it is not permanent and is reduced by cutting down tea, coffee and red wine. Professional scaling and polishing may be needed.

src.q: Discoloration of the teeth and tongue may occur. The stain is not permanent
In certain cases professional treatment (scaling and polishing) may be required to remove the stain completely.

items.t: Transient taste disturbance and numbness, tingling or burning of the tongue may occur at first; these usually lessen with continued use.

src.q: Transient disturbances of taste sensation and a numbness, tingling or burning sensation of the tongue may occur on initial use of the mouthwash.
These effects usually diminish with continued use.

items.t: Contains macrogolglycerol hydroxystearate, which may cause skin reactions.

src.q: Macrogolglycerol hydroxystearate may cause skin reactions

items.t: Incompatible with anionic agents, which are usually present in ordinary toothpastes: use toothpaste first, rinse the mouth, or use it at a different time of day.

src.q: Chlorhexidine is incompatible with anionic agents.
These should therefore be used before Corsodyl 0.2% Mouthwash (rinsing the mouth between applications) or at a different time of day.

renal.note: Neither UK 0.2% mouthwash SmPC gives renal advice. Both state chlorhexidine is very poorly absorbed with no detectable blood levels after oral use.

hepatic.note: Neither UK 0.2% mouthwash SmPC gives hepatic advice.

items.t: No evidence of adverse effects on the fetus; the SmPC recommends no special precautions.

src.q: There is no evidence of any adverse effects on the foetus arising from the use of chlorhexidine digluconate during pregnancy or on infants during lactation.
Therefore no special precautions are recommended.

items.t: No evidence of adverse effects on breastfed infants; no special precautions recommended.

src.q: There is no evidence of any adverse effects on the foetus arising from the use of chlorhexidine digluconate during pregnancy or on infants during lactation.
Therefore no special precautions are recommended.

reproductive.note: The UK 0.2% mouthwash SmPCs give no fertility or contraception information.

items.t: Very common: coated tongue. Common: dry mouth, loss or change of taste, sore tongue, oral tingling or numbness.

src.q: Very Common: Tongue coated Common: Dry mouth
Common: Aguesia / dysguesia Glossodynia Oral paraesthesia / hypoaesthesia

items.t: Isolated reports: tooth and tongue discoloration, mouth irritation, peeling or swelling of the oral mucosa, parotid gland swelling.

src.q: Isolated reports: Discoloration of the teeth and tongue
Desquamation / swelling of oral mucosa (see section 4.4) Parotid gland swelling

items.t: Hypersensitivity and anaphylaxis (isolated reports). If swelling or difficulty breathing occurs, stop and seek immediate medical help.

src.q: Hypersensitivity and anaphylaxis (see section 4.3 and 4.4)
In case of swelling or difficulty breathing, stop using the product and seek immediate medical help.

items.t: Stop and seek advice if the mouth becomes sore, swollen or irritated.

src.q: In case of soreness, swelling or irritation of the mouth, stop using the product and consult a healthcare professional.

items.t: If taste disturbance or tongue numbness/burning persists, seek advice.

src.q: If the condition persists, consult a healthcare professional.

items.t: Rinse for about 1 minute and spit out; do not swallow. Use toothpaste before the mouthwash (rinse between) or at a different time of day.

src.q: Thoroughly rinse the mouth for about one minute with 10 ml twice daily. Spit out after use.
is incompatible with anionic agents which are usually present in conventional dentifrices

items.t: Teeth and tongue may stain brown; cutting down tea, coffee and red wine helps. Denture stain can be removed with a normal denture cleaner.

src.q: can largely be prevented by reducing the consumption of dietary chromagens such as tea, coffee or red wine
In the case of dentures this can be prevented by cleaning with a conventional denture cleaner.

items.t: Stop at once and get urgent help if there is swelling or difficulty breathing.

src.q: In case of swelling or difficulty breathing, stop using the product and seek immediate medical help.

rules.consequence: Chlorhexidine can cause generalised allergic reactions and anaphylactic shock.
rules.action: Do not use. MHRA: do not give any chlorhexidine-containing product to anyone with a possible history of allergic reaction to chlorhexidine.

src.q: is contraindicated for patients who have previously shown a hypersensitivity reaction to Chlorhexidine or to any of the excipients in the formulation
chlorhexidine is known to induce hypersensitivity, including generalised allergic reactions and anaphylactic shock
Products or medical devices containing chlorhexidine should not be administered to anyone with a possible history of an allergic reaction to chlorhexidine.

rules.consequence: The licensed dose applies to adults and children 12 years and over.
rules.action: Should not be used under 12 years unless recommended by a healthcare professional.
rules.sourceWording: should not use the product unless recommended by a healthcare professional

src.q: Children under 12 years of age should not use the product unless recommended by a healthcare professional.

rules.consequence: No evidence of adverse effects on the foetus from chlorhexidine digluconate.

src.q: There is no evidence of any adverse effects on the foetus arising from the use of chlorhexidine digluconate during pregnancy or on infants during lactation.
Therefore no special precautions are recommended.

rules.consequence: No evidence of adverse effects on breastfed infants from chlorhexidine digluconate.

src.q: There is no evidence of any adverse effects on the foetus arising from the use of chlorhexidine digluconate during pregnancy or on infants during lactation.
Therefore no special precautions are recommended.
